NEW YORK CITY —  Yesterday, over 25 ICE vehicles descended on Queens — for 10+ hours, rapid responders fended off ICE and did not witness a single abduction. In response, Rebecca Rodriguez, Co-Director of Hands Off NYC, released the following statement: 


“Yesterday, over 25 known ICE vehicles infiltrated East Elmhurst and surrounding neighborhoods in Queens, and for over ten hours, neighbors showed up, blowing whistles, documenting, and alerting the community. Meanwhile, ICE’s violent tactics were on full display — agents ran neighbors over with their cars, repeatedly threatened to use pepper spray on neighbors who were documenting, and drove the wrong direction on one-way residential streets, going double or triple the speed limit.


This was one of the largest ICE operations New York has faced since both Canal Street incidents in fall of 2025, and yesterday, for all ten hours, responders didn’t see ICE make a single abduction. Over the past year, Hands Off NYC has trained over 10,000 New Yorkers to know their rights and how to spot ICE. Alongside community groups and concerned neighbors, we’ve seen this work pay off. When we show up and exercise our constitutional rights, ICE leaves.
